summary: cro checked in 1 executive handoff item(s)

items.summary: CRO disposition: preserve containment-only execution and retain the following as deferred opportunities, not proposals or queue work. 1) Fleet CTA/accessibility primitive: shadcn-ui/ui is MIT, lab-supported, and passed 3/3 bounded checks; smallest prototype is one isolated static CTA rendered without adding the dependency. Use case: reusable conversion surfaces on affiliate and editorial sites. Risks: dependency supply chain, Astro/Cloudflare integration, bundle weight, and no demonstrated conversion lift. Metric: CTA interaction rate; time-to-learn: 14 days after an authorized implementation. 2) Content-ingestion prototype: microsoft/markitdown is MIT, lab-supported, and passed 8/8 bounded checks. Use case: convert approved source documents into reviewable Markdown for SEO workflows. Smallest prototype: one offline fixture conversion with provenance and human review. Risks: source rights, parser fidelity, prompt/content contamination, maintenance and dependency review. Metric: reviewer-accepted output rate and time saved; time-to-learn: one controlled batch. 3) Static explanatory diagrams: mermaid-js/mermaid is MIT and lab-supported, but no native checks were available without dependency installation. Use case: explain research, product flows, or guides. Smallest prototype: one manually authored isolated SVG artifact with sanitization and accessibility review. Risks: SVG sanitization, page weight, accessibility, renderer maintenance, and no proven SEO or conversion impact. Metric: engaged time or CTA interaction only if existing telemetry already captures it; time-to-learn: 14 days after authorization. 4) Existing SEO and affiliate opportunities remain site-specific backlog, including high-impression pages and affiliate click-through surfaces already recorded by SEO and revenue systems. Do not infer revenue from impressions, clicks, sessions, conversions, or AI cost; available affiliate revenue is aggregate and not site-attributable. Any future prototype requires documented ownership, root cause, deduplication, deterministic validation, rollback, consent/disclosure preservation, and an existing measurement window. No new dependencies, telemetry, spending, credentials, domains, deployments, experiments, or monetization changes are recommended this cycle.
